hard_guards: Do not require a Bank for normal Algebra Demos/Investigations builds.
Do not turn Practice/Bank question routes into Investigation worksheets by default.
Do not let optional resources become sole required core instruction/evidence.
Final delivery is a real ZIP.
Demo slide dependencies may not rely on memory or repeated carry-forward boxes: explicitly have students copy/record needed evidence, then use their notes on later slides.
Every Demo ends with a short discussion set and the Demo teacher guide supplies slide-by-slide replicas plus suggested/acceptable responses.

Investigation teacher guides preserve the practical overview/Strong Synthesis, then provide answered/rationale walkthroughs for substantive tasks, and end with a student-style synthesis replica plus acceptable responses/rationale.
Demos/Investigations are authoring resources and may invoke the Framework graph tool; inspect the capability inventory before manually inventing supported visuals.

Stable HTML/CSS shells do not justify repeated student actions. Choose movement, building, data collection, four-view connection, graph/model analysis, critique, creation, or other section-fit modes from the Algebra profile.
PLAN-FIRST GATE: create and QA the complete section-by-section plan before writing any Demo/Investigation student or teacher HTML.
Package ~demos_investigations_build_plan.json and ~demos_investigations_build_plan.html so the design map is inspectable and editable later.
Rendering is downstream of the plan: planned movement, data collection, making/building, gallery/sort, graph/model, or create/trade experiences may not collapse into generic two-task worksheets.

Every section has an explicit graph decision; for Algebra, near-zero graph/model use across graph-heavy topics is a planning failure unless students are intentionally constructing those representations themselves.
